# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book should not exist.
There are already so many free available materials online.
Many universities have materials and open courses (examples).
There are PDF and books available.
There are videos on YouTube, some might be more legitimate than others.
I also hope that there are libraries where you are and you have access to recent up-to-date physical books...if you are student do not hesitate to make a request to your advisors and acquaintances, still stay reasonable.
As far as know, foreign researchers are not shy on bringing knowledge. Just ask!!!
And ultimately, I expect that the major part of what is written here are taught during undergraduate and graduate courses at your institutions.

So is there a need for this book? Well, I aim and try to address superficial problems with this book.
The first problem is **decentralized information**.
Maybe there is a book on coding and another book on statistics.
Maybe in some books, the basics are not covered so you need to look somewhere else.
Maybe the levels differ.
The first aim to gather in one place multiple informations, maybe this handbook has an encyclopedia philosophy.
As such it is expected to grow in time.
<!-- This early realize for instance includes basic knowledge, with beginner level. basic math vs intermediate math, descriptive statistics vs statistical inference etc. -->

<!--
This cover topics that I feel are not understood (essentially basics) or most commonly used without reflection (say PCA or ANOVA).
Starts with a basic level, maybe at most intermediate level.
I expect it to grow and be updated overtime although I cannot guarantee the regularity of the update/release.
Hopefully, this will also include more advanced topics in the future.
Although as above, if you look for advanced, maybe this is not the book for you. -->

Second, **dense and formality**.
This is heavy focus on practical/applied side.
Text book and example can be dense with formal stuff. This is about inutition, examples, and code, and tips. There is section on formal definition but it is there for the most curious ones, and also a concrete bridge to the and the intuition.
That can simply be googled.
When add in the last section called tips and warnings: fun useful important.
Tnis is also a compact and self-taught.

Third, **western perspective** that might not align.
For instance, using feet vs metric system. or everyday is mostly imaginary for us, taking a metro or a train.
This is for Malagasy in mind.
After teaching workshops for over a decade, there are many things barriers.
Malagasy struggle with.
This is a collection of those things.
Also, intution is based on context in Madagascar, and examples, and metaphors with Malagasy flavor.
Not sure because Malagasy is also a heterogenous.
Some Malagasy terms are kept on purpose because the English translation is more confusing.
And to be clear, shortcuting, it is my "Malagasy", I can't speak for them.

The final problem is **access**.
This is but if one finds this interesting, it is free.
This is free book, you can download it from principally my webpage and probably other pages.
There are two versions. I recommend html for nicer formatting.
But if internet is an issue, a PDF also exist but and many features are lost (that is why publisher)
Feel free to share it with anyone, use on whatever you want but this is self-edited book so you should not use it as a valid citation.
As the proverb says, *Saonjo iray lohasa, tsy laozan'izay mamara*.
Someone might try to make a business out of it. I am sorry for those who will pay for it and get scammed.

As a warning, it is worth mentioning that I am no expert in any of the topics and sections.
I am mostly self-taught training in statistics and programming.
There are experts in the field, and I should be the absolute reference.
This book is based on my own experience and the way how I understand the concept, the way how I code.
This is more a generalist approach to the concept to converse with mathematician, statisticians, programmers, data scientist. As I am not sure I failed, but I am not confident I succeeded.
<!-- Yet, to enhance the value, I had colleagues and past advisors--the experts--that made sure that what is written is not completely nonsense.
I am grateful and forever in dept to Otso, Tony, Guillaume, Gavin, Eva.
However, if there is something wrong, I take full responsibility. -->

What about on AI: AI is another blooming stuff and seems like a obvious approach.
First, I used AI to help polishing the book, some codes where written by AI, and even some examples.
Second, there is chance you can simply google, that is a nice augmented value.
Third,this is above critical thinking, altough I try to simplify. Using AI to bypass is loosing the needed training.
Fourth, philosopical...but I am not sure where it is. As this is foundational. Several times I asked AI and checked by human so hopefully is not obsolete yet.


How this book is structured
- Intuition (free form)
- Definition (edited from wikipedia) condensed for lisibility. No need to reinvent the wheel
- Examples
- Tips and warning
  - Semantic:
  - R behavior.

This is R, and code, output.
Don't be frustrated if repetitive,(one concept in anther chapter). This is part of learning but also, there is no expectation that you will read each chapter, so reminded as it appears

### Preface to version 0.5: beta {.unnumbered}
Teraka ihany ambatobevohoka. This has been a long process, mostly thinking about the format, howt o structure the chapters and how to link them. This version is essentially the raw beginner version. Many will be underwhelmed to not say dissapointed, including me, by the selection of chapters, but I think it is time to publish for the following reasons

- Is it going the right direction...your feedback is direly needed. It will help greatly whether it is constructive or destructive comments. This first release 0.5 is mostly about basic topics and still in english. I think it would be useful to have a first sense, and depending on time and availability, I will do the full release 1.0 in the near future.

- During most workshops, the first few days are crucial yet condense. So at minimum, it is basic and having a pause between digesting and learning about diversity metrics and community ecology, inferential stats, theoretical ecology.

- Semantic and terminology: mostly address across parts

- Apologies if the text reads like AI but maybe it is good enough, this is also an experimental phase, text editing can consume and not sure if this is where time should be invested Expect when I have time to re-humanize the text.

On can see this book as software version (hence version than edition). I will gradually expect to from time to time. They will be 0.5.x...hopefully it is not long until the version 1.0 is out.
